ingredients.title: Welcome and working agreement
ingredients.description: Introduce yourself, explain the purpose and length of the meeting, confidentiality and its limits. Ask what the person expects.

ingredients.title: Opening round
ingredients.description: Each participant says in one or two sentences what they bring today. The facilitator does not comment, only thanks.

ingredients.title: Mood weather
ingredients.description: Participants describe their mood as weather (sun, fog, storm). Good for young people and groups reluctant to talk about feelings.

ingredients.title: HALT check-in
ingredients.description: Quick check: am I hungry, angry, lonely, tired? Helps notice states that raise the risk of relapse.

ingredients.title: Open questions and reflections
ingredients.description: Ask questions that cannot be answered “yes/no” and reflect back what you hear. Aim for more reflections than questions.

ingredients.title: Readiness ruler
ingredients.description: The person marks on a 0–10 scale how important change is and how confident they are. Follow up: “Why that number and not lower?”

ingredients.title: Decisional balance
ingredients.description: Fill in the matrix together: benefits and costs of the current behaviour and of change. End with a summary of what speaks for change.

ingredients.title: Eliciting change talk
ingredients.description: Ask about desire, ability, reasons and need for change (“What would be better if…?”). Reinforce every statement about change.

ingredients.title: Looking forward
ingredients.description: Ask what life might look like in a year if nothing changes, and if the change succeeds. Do not judge the answers.

ingredients.title: Change plan
ingredients.description: When the person is ready, write together: what I want to change, why, first steps, who will help me, how I will know I am progressing.

ingredients.title: Chain analysis
ingredients.description: Reconstruct a specific situation step by step: trigger, thoughts, emotions, behaviour, consequences. Look for links where a different choice was possible.

ingredients.title: Thought record
ingredients.description: Write down the situation, automatic thought, emotion and its intensity. Identify the distortion and look for a more balanced thought.

ingredients.title: Trigger map
ingredients.description: The person marks people, places, states and situations that trigger the urge to use. Match coping strategies to the strongest ones.

ingredients.title: Scaling and the miracle question
ingredients.description: Ask where the person is today on a 0–10 scale and what would move them one point up. You can add the miracle question.

ingredients.title: Refusal skills training
ingredients.description: Go through the steps of assertive refusal (a clear “no”, a reason without over-explaining, an alternative, leaving the situation) and practise them.

ingredients.title: Assertive “I” message
ingredients.description: Participants practise the formula: “When…, I feel…, because…, I would like…”. Use examples from their own lives.

ingredients.title: Role-play with a situation card
ingredients.description: Draw a situation card, assign roles and observers. After the scene discuss what worked and repeat it with improvements.

ingredients.title: Step-by-step problem solving
ingredients.description: Define the problem, list possible solutions without judging, weigh pros and cons, choose one and plan the first step.

ingredients.title: Group contract
ingredients.description: The group agrees on rules together (e.g. confidentiality, speaking for oneself, the right to pass). The rules are written down and accepted by all.

ingredients.title: Movement energiser
ingredients.description: A short movement game (e.g. “Change places if you like…”) that releases tension and energises the group.

ingredients.title: Trust exercise
ingredients.description: A pair exercise building trust (e.g. guiding a partner with closed eyes). Always with the option to opt out and a debrief.

ingredients.title: Small-group discussion
ingredients.description: Split the group into teams of 3–4 with a specific question and time limit. Teams present their conclusions to everyone.

ingredients.title: Family genogram
ingredients.description: Draw a three-generation family tree together, marking relationships, key events and patterns (e.g. drinking, violence, strengths).

ingredients.title: Family communication exercise
ingredients.description: Family members take turns speaking about one issue while the other paraphrases before replying. The facilitator ensures people speak for themselves, not accuse.

ingredients.title: Support map
ingredients.description: The person places people and institutions who can help around themselves according to closeness. Look for gaps and new sources of support.

ingredients.title: Family strengths
ingredients.description: Each family member names one thing they value about the family and one thing they do well together.

ingredients.title: Normative quiz
ingredients.description: Pupils estimate what percentage of peers drink or smoke, then compare with survey data. Discuss where the differences come from.

ingredients.title: Myths and facts
ingredients.description: Teams get statements about substances and decide: myth or fact. The facilitator explains factually, without scaring.

ingredients.title: Life-skills scenario
ingredients.description: Groups work on a short story about a peer in a difficult situation (party, pressure, exam stress) and suggest solutions.

ingredients.title: Advert analysis
ingredients.description: Pupils analyse an alcohol or e-cigarette advert: who it targets, what it promises, what it leaves out.

ingredients.title: Breathing exercise
ingredients.description: Guided breathing in a steady rhythm (e.g. 4–4–4–4) for a few minutes. Good at the start, after a difficult part or at the end.

ingredients.title: Grounding 5-4-3-2-1
ingredients.description: The person names 5 things they see, 4 they touch, 3 they hear, 2 they smell and 1 taste. Helps return to the here and now.

ingredients.title: Urge surfing
ingredients.description: The person rates the craving 0–10, observes it like a wave that rises and falls while breathing calmly, then rates it again.

ingredients.title: Summary
ingredients.description: Summarise the main themes and agreements in your own words, then ask whether anything is missing.

ingredients.title: Between-session task
ingredients.description: Agree together on one small, specific task until the next meeting (e.g. noting triggers).

ingredients.title: Closing round
ingredients.description: Everyone completes the sentence: “Today I'm taking away…”. You can add a quick rating of the session.

ingredients.title: Agreeing the next step
ingredients.description: Agree the date of the next meeting and what happens until then. Remind the person of crisis contacts.

sessionTemplates.title: First meeting
sessionTemplates.goal: Building the relationship, agreeing how to work together and an initial understanding of the person's situation.
sessionTemplates.audience: Individual meeting, young people or adults

sessionTemplates.title: Motivational conversation
sessionTemplates.goal: Strengthening motivation for change by exploring ambivalence and eliciting change talk.

sessionTemplates.title: Chain analysis
sessionTemplates.goal: Understanding the course of a specific incident (e.g. a relapse) and finding points where a different response is possible.
sessionTemplates.audience: Individual meeting after an incident or relapse

sessionTemplates.title: Socio-therapeutic session
sessionTemplates.goal: Providing corrective relational experiences and practising social skills in a safe group.

sessionTemplates.title: Social skills training
sessionTemplates.goal: Learning and practising a selected skill (refusal, assertiveness, conflict resolution).

sessionTemplates.title: Family session
sessionTemplates.goal: Improving family communication, identifying strengths and agreeing shared steps of support.

sessionTemplates.title: Classroom prevention lesson
sessionTemplates.goal: Correcting normative beliefs and practising decision-making – interactively, without scare tactics.

sessionTemplates.title: Relapse prevention
sessionTemplates.goal: Identifying high-risk situations and practising ways to cope with cravings.

sociotherapy.title: Socio-therapeutic programme “Easier Together” – template
goals: building a sense of safety and belonging in the group
recognising and naming emotions and ways to express them
developing communication, cooperation and assertiveness skills
groupRules: What we say in the group stays in the group (except when someone is in danger).
We speak for ourselves and about ourselves.
We don't judge or mock others.
Everyone has the right to pass.
We come on time and sober.

cycle.title: Getting to know each other
cycle.aims: Group bonding and agreeing the group contract.

cycle.title: Emotions – what do I feel?
activities: talk about where in the body we feel emotions

cycle.title: Anger and how to handle it
cycle.aims: Learning safe ways to express anger.
activities: list of ways to calm down

cycle.title: Communication
cycle.aims: Practising active listening and the “I” message.

cycle.title: Assertiveness and refusal
cycle.aims: Practising refusal and defending one's boundaries.

cycle.title: Peer pressure
cycle.aims: Recognising pressure and ways to stay independent.

cycle.title: Farewell and what next
cycle.aims: Summing up, recognising change, closing the group.
activities: letter to myself in six months

readaptationAreas.title: Housing
items: establish where the person will live in the first days
check whether returning to family or previous housing is possible
if needed, apply for a place in a shelter, night shelter or training/supported flat
apply for municipal (social) housing
check rent arrears and options to repay or work them off

readaptationAreas.title: Documents
items: ID card – apply for or collect
registration of residence (meldunek) at the current address
release certificate and report from the prison or facility
school certificates, diplomas, course certificates
employment history and social insurance (ZUS) documents (e.g. to establish work record)
disability card or certificate – if applicable

readaptationAreas.title: Work and education
items: register with the district labour office as unemployed or job-seeking
prepare a CV and practise a job interview
look into options for people leaving prison (e.g. social cooperatives, social integration centres)
continue education or a vocational course
financial plan for the first month

readaptationAreas.title: Health and addiction treatment
items: national health insurance (NFZ) – check or register (e.g. via the labour office or social welfare centre)
choose a primary care doctor
book an appointment at an addiction treatment clinic or continue therapy
contact a support group or mutual-help fellowship (e.g. AA, NA)
relapse prevention plan for the first weeks
continue any prescribed treatment according to the doctor's documentation

readaptationAreas.title: Relationships
items: establish which family members and friends can be contacted
plan a conversation with the family about rules and expectations
identify relationships that raise the risk of reoffending or using
contact with children – check court arrangements
find at least one trusted person to contact in a crisis

readaptationAreas.title: Institutional support
items: contact with the probation officer (if supervision was ordered) – date of the first meeting
visit the social welfare centre (OPS/MOPS) – benefits, material help, social work
check eligibility for help from the Justice Fund (post-release support)
contact an NGO that supports people after release
free legal aid – debts, maintenance, fines
list of phone numbers and addresses with opening hours

goalExamples: the family knows the available forms of help and where to go
parents agree shared, clear rules at home
family members talk about difficulties without blaming
the family member looks after their own health and rest
the family has a safety plan for a crisis or violence
the family reinforces the loved one's sober behaviour (CRAFT approach)
the child has regular contact with a trusted adult outside the home
supportExamples: consultations at the municipal counselling point
support group for family members (e.g. Al-Anon, groups at clinics)
therapy for family members at an addiction treatment clinic
family assistant from the social welfare centre
the “Blue Card” procedure and interdisciplinary team in cases of violence
